'''Robert Calvin Armstrong''' is an American chemical engineer known for his work in [[rheology]] and non-Newtonian fluid mechanics. He served as director of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] Energy Initiative from 2013 to 2023 and is the Chevron Professor of Chemical Engineering, emeritus, at MIT.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Robert Armstrong
 |website=MIT Energy Initiative
 |url=https://energy.mit.edu/profile/robert-armstrong/
 |access-date=2026-04-19
}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Armstrong received a Bachelor of Chemical Engineering degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1970 and a PhD in chemical engineering from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1973.<ref name="AIChE">{{cite web |title=Robert C. Armstrong |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/bio/robert-c-armstrong |website=AIChE |date=20 March 2012 |access-date=9 March 2021}}</ref>

He joined the MIT faculty in 1973, and he served as head of the Department of [[Chemical Engineering]] from 1996 to 2007. From 2013 to 2023, Armstrong served as director of the [[MIT Energy Initiative]] (MITEI), after having been the organization's initial deputy director from its founding in 2007.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Robert Armstrong
 |website=MIT Energy Initiative
 |url=https://energy.mit.edu/profile/robert-armstrong/
 |access-date=2026-04-19
}}</ref>

Armstrong's research has focused on polymer fluid mechanics and the rheology of complex materials.<ref name="AIChE" /> He co-authored the two-volume textbook ''Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids'': ''Vol. 1: Fluid Mechanics'' with R. B. Bird and O. Hassager, and ''Vol. 2: Kinetic Theory'' with R. B. Bird, C. F. Curtiss, and O. Hassager.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bird |first1=R. B. |last2=Armstrong |first2=R. C. |last3=Hassager |first3=O. |title=Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids, Vol. 1: Fluid Mechanics |edition=2nd |publisher=Wiley |location=New York |year=1987}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Bird |first1=R. B. |last2=Curtiss |first2=C. F. |last3=Armstrong |first3=R. C. |last4=Hassager |first4=O. |title=Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids, Vol. 2: Kinetic Theory |edition=2nd |publisher=Wiley |location=New York |year=1987}}</ref>

==Honors==
Armstrong received the [[Bingham Medal]] from the [[Society of Rheology]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Robert C. Armstrong - 2006 Bingham Medalist
 |website=The Society of Rheology
 |date=2006-01-01
 |url=https://www.societyofrheology.org/awards/robert-c-armstrong-2006-bingham-medalist
 |access-date=2026-04-19
}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2008 for “conducting outstanding research on non-Newtonian fluid mechanics, co-authoring landmark textbooks, and providing leadership in chemical engineering education.”<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Robert C. Armstrong|url=https://nae.edu/31020/Dr-Robert-C-Armstrong|access-date=2021-01-08|website=National Academy of Engineering}}</ref> In 2020, he became a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert C. Armstrong|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/robert-c-armstrong|access-date=2021-01-08|website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|language=en}}</ref>
